scope: Theorem 1.1 of the manuscript “A Polynomial-Time Algorithm for Three-Machine Unit-Job Scheduling” (preprints/A-polynomial-time-algorithm-for-three-machine-unit-job-scheduling-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 124 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 2080c4ad5953f225), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 2. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let an explicitly listed finite directed acyclic graph specify the precedence constraints on n ≥ 1 nonpreemptive unit-length jobs on three identical machines. There is a uniform deterministic algorithm that constructs a feasible schedule of minimum makespan. Given also an integer deadline 1 ≤ T ≤ n, it decides feasibility exactly and returns a schedule whenever the answer is affirmative. Both tasks can be performed in O((L + 2)150020) steps on a deterministic multitape Turing machine, where L is the total binary input length.
